item.title: New kids on the block: London's hotel boom and the new openings around the world to have on your radar
item.description: From Scotland to the Seychelles, there are myriad new hotel openings this year to inspire your travels.

item.title: 'To my unspeakable disgust and pain, the little inconsiderate beast squirted his acid down my throat': The army of animals weaponising chemistry in the fight for survival
item.description: Clouds of noxious gas, stink bombs and purple smokescreens may sound like schoolboy pranks, but the animal world is just as capable of executing arresting chemical warfare.

item.title: How well do you really know Country Life? Test your knowledge of your favourite magazine in Quiz of the Day, February 6, 2026
item.description: It's Friday and we're feeling narcissistic so this quiz is all about... us.

item.title: When is a cottage not a cottage? When it's a spectacular, glass-walled lakehouse making waves in 'Heated Rivalry'
item.description: The television show 'Heated Rivalry' has become such a huge hit that the phrase 'coming to the cottage' has found a whole new definition. But does that spell trouble for those who still think of a cottage as an ancient stone-built home with a thatched roof? Will Hosie investigates.

item.title: 'I was utterly bewitched': The heartwarming success story of one of Britain's greatest rose-growers
item.description: Charles Quest-Ritson talks to Trevor White, whose Norfolk rose nursery is sought out by enthusiasts for the quality and variety of its stock. Photographs by Richard Bloom.

item.title: ‘I don't consider myself to be a nepo baby at all’: Caroline Avedon on preserving her grandfather's legacy — and her consuming passions
item.description: Caroline initially wanted to be a lawyer, but now that she works for Richard Avedon’s foundation, she can’t imagine doing anything else, finds Lotte Brundle.

item.title: Lodge Park: Megève is where snow and style mingle, and this hotel is at the heart of it all
item.description: Refurbished, refreshed, renewed: Five-star Lodge Park is a comforting, luxurious and elegant treat in the snow-capped Alps.

item.title: 'It’s harder with someone who says yes to everything’: What it's like having a bespoke scent made by one of London's oldest perfumers
item.description: Scent is the most romantic of the senses, some say. Lotte Brundle heads to Floris in London, ahead of Valentine’s Day, to have a bespoke perfume made for her.

item.title: The Norfolk home of the grandmother of Diana, Princess of Wales, has come to the market
item.description: Lady Fermoy's former home Uphall is on the market, with 11 bedrooms, endless charm and a Victorian swimming pond in the gardens.

item.title: Repton: The 500-year-old school with a medieval priory whose story leads back to the kings of Mercia
item.description: The medieval Augustinian priory within the curtilage of Repton School in Derbyshire links together the history of this great public school with the Anglo-Saxon era and the Kings of Mercia. David Robinson tells its story, with photographs by Paul Highnam for Country Life.
